title: Association of volatile organic compound metabolites with hearing loss: unveiling their potential mechanism and intervention target.
authors: Zhou, Jingcheng; Sun, Guanchao; Zhao, Houming; Qin, Handai; Bi, Yiming; Chen, Xuemin
one_liner_zh: 该文研究挥发性有机化合物代谢物与听力损失的关联，涉及转录因子网络和分子对接，但核心对象非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题无关。
abstract: Hearing loss (HL) is an otolaryngology disease susceptible to environmental pollutants. Volatile organic compounds (VOCs), as a class of chemical pollutants with evaporation propensity, pose a great threat to human health. However, the association between VOCs and HL remains unclear. This study aimed to explore the association between urinary-specific VOC metabolites and HL. It included 1048 participants from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2011 to 2012. Multivariate linear regression models, smooth curve analysis, and stratified analysis were employed to investigate the relationship between urinary-specific VOC metabolite concentrations and pure tone audiometry (PTA) across three different frequencies. A two-piecewise linear regression model was employed to analyze the threshold effects of urinary-specific VOC metabolites on hearing threshold changes. Furthermore, a comparative toxicogenomics database (CTD) and functional gene enrichment were constructed. An interaction network of transcription factors, genes, and non-coding RNA was constructed to further confirm the upstream and downstream regulatory relationships. Molecular docking analyses were conducted to explore the potential binding modes and critical docking sites. Additionally, a moderation analysis was conducted to investigate the role of oxidative stress in moderating the influence of VOC metabolites on hearing. Multivariate linear regression model discerned a significant correlation between cyanide 2-aminothiazoline-4-carboxylic acid (ATCA) with speech-frequency PTA and N-acetyl-S-(3,4-dihydroxybutyl)-L-cysteine (DHBMA) with high-frequency PTA. The smoothed curve and threshold effect analysis corroborated a positive linear relationship between cyanide ATCA and speech-frequency PTA without a threshold effect only in the 20-34 age group. Additionally, the bioinformatics analysis discovered pathogenic genes related to cyanide-induced HL and suggested that oxidative stress responses play a critical role in this biological process. Furthermore, the moderation effect of total bilirubin (TB), an oxidative stress-associated molecule, was ascertained on the effects of ATCA on hearing. Our findings suggest a potential link between VOC metabolites and hearing and indicate the crucial role of oxidative stress responses in this association.
abstract_zh: 听力损失（HL）是一种易受环境污染物影响的耳鼻咽喉科疾病。挥发性有机化合物（VOCs）作为一类具有蒸发倾向的化学污染物，对人类健康构成重大威胁。然而，VOCs与HL之间的关联仍不明确。本研究旨在探讨尿液中特异性VOC代谢物与HL之间的关联。研究纳入了2011至2012年间来自国家健康与营养调查（NHANES）的1048名参与者。采用多元线性回归模型、平滑曲线分析和分层分析，研究尿液中特异性VOC代谢物浓度与三个不同频率下纯音测听（PTA）之间的关系。采用两段线性回归模型分析尿液中特异性VOC代谢物对听力阈值变化的阈值效应。此外，构建了比较毒物基因组学数据库（CTD）和功能基因富集分析。构建了转录因子、基因和非编码RNA的相互作用网络，以进一步确认上下游调控关系。进行了分子对接分析，以探索潜在的结合模式和关键对接位点。另外，进行了调节效应分析，以研究氧化应激在调节VOC代谢物对听力影响中的作用。多元线性回归模型发现氰化物2-氨基噻唑啉-4-羧酸（ATCA）与言语频率PTA以及N-乙酰-S-(3,4-二羟基丁基)-L-半胱氨酸（DHBMA）与高频PTA之间存在显著相关性。平滑曲线和阈值效应分析证实，仅在20-34岁年龄组中，氰化物ATCA与言语频率PTA之间存在正线性关系，且无阈值效应。此外，生物信息学分析发现了与氰化物诱导的HL相关的致病基因，并提示氧化应激反应在这一生物学过程中发挥关键作用。进一步地，总胆红素（TB）作为氧化应激相关分子的调节效应在ATCA对听力的影响中得到确认。我们的研究结果表明，VOC代谢物与听力之间存在潜在关联，并指出氧化应激反应在这一关联中的关键作用。
